sealed: Written and committed after organ 1b was measured (receipts/organ-1b.json, commit 64057e1) and before the strict schema check or tools/measure-1c.mjs existed. Disclosed: designed after seeing B1 fail. P0 checked the structure the judge needs but not every field's type, so a garbage member id, or a garbage 'by' on an event nothing reads, passed cleanly (3 records); and organ 1b's measurement used null as its 'no record yet' marker, so 16 null records were never judged. B1's failed verdict is kept.
what: Organ 1c makes P0 strict: every field of the record, schema v1, has a type, and a field that is present must have it. The record: schema, job_id, member_id (non-empty text), harness (name; version text if given), models (a list of text), intent (goal; constraints, success criteria, allowed tools and out of scope as lists of text; sealed_at a time; hash 64 lower-case hex), timeline, artifacts (id, role input or output, sha256 text, stored true or false), claims (id, text, evidence a list of pointers each naming where and which, criterion text if given), summary (five words or more). Each timeline entry: seq a whole number from 0, rising; at a time; kind one of the ten; and the fields of its kind typed (a tool use names its tool, an assumption says whether it was surfaced, an answer says which question it answers, and so on); 'by', on any entry that has it, is human, agent or independent. A new entry point, assessStrict(), is rubric v3: the strict P0, then the ten checks. judge() (v1) and assess() (v2) are unchanged, so organs 1 and 1b still reproduce.
suite: Fresh damaged records, seeds 290000 on (none used before), made by the same kinds of damage as before and each checked to differ from its clean source, with the marker bug fixed: a record that is null, or any other value, is judged. Organ 1's clean and planted jobs are judged again under rubric v3.

claims.claim: No damaged record passes cleanly: of 2,000 fresh damaged records, each differing from its clean source, none is judged a pass on all eleven checks under rubric v3, and none throws.

Most damage is caught by the schema itself: at least 95% of the 2,000 fail the strict P0. (Some damage leaves a record valid but incomplete, an empty list of claims for instance; C1 says those still do not pass cleanly.)

The strict schema costs nothing on good records: it passes all 500 clean and all 500 planted jobs (a badly run job is not a malformed record), the other ten checks give the same outcomes as under rubric v1 on every one of them, and every judgement is the same twice.
The earlier holes are closed: the 3 damaged records organ 1b judged a clean pass, made again from their seeds, fail the strict P0; and every null record among the fresh damage is judged and fails P0.
